title: Advanced Business Idioms
completion_message: ¡Fenomenal! Los modismos corporativos o 'Business Idioms' son el dialecto secreto de los ejecutivos y directivos. Frases como 'Boil the ocean' o 'Move the needle' te permiten comunicarte con la agilidad y el estilo de un hablante nativo en la alta gerencia.

parts.visual:
En reuniones corporativas, los ejecutivos nativos hablan constantemente en metáforas e 'idioms'. Aquí tienes los más avanzados: 

1. Move the needle (Hacer una diferencia notable / Mover la aguja): 
- Lograr un cambio que se nota en los resultados o ganancias. 
Ej: This marketing campaign is nice, but it won't MOVE THE NEEDLE on our total revenue. 

2. Boil the ocean (Intentar hacer lo imposible / Abarcar demasiado): 
- Tratar de completar una tarea tan grande o compleja que es imposible o ineficiente. 
Ej: Let's focus on one specific market first; there's no need to BOIL THE OCEAN. 

3. Push the envelope (Ir más allá de los límites / Innovar): 
- Superar los límites actuales de lo posible o lo normal. 
Ej: As a tech company, we must constantly PUSH THE ENVELOPE.
parts.audio: Welcome to Advanced Business Idioms. In corporate meetings, native executives constantly speak in metaphors. Number 1: Move the needle. This means to make a noticeable difference, especially in revenue or results. For example: This marketing campaign is nice, but it won't MOVE THE NEEDLE on our total revenue. Number 2: Boil the ocean. This means trying to do something so difficult or broad that it's impossible. For example: Let's focus on one specific market first; there's no need to BOIL THE OCEAN. Number 3: Push the envelope. To go beyond the current limits or innovate. For example: As a tech company, we must constantly PUSH THE ENVELOPE.

parts.visual:
4. Get the ball rolling (Poner las cosas en marcha / Empezar): 
- Iniciar un proceso o proyecto. 
Ej: Let's GET THE BALL ROLLING on the new software update. 

5. Kick the can down the road (Posponer un problema difícil): 
- Evitar tomar una decisión difícil, dejándola para el futuro. 
Ej: The politicians didn't solve the debt crisis; they just KICKED THE CAN DOWN THE ROAD. 

6. Circle back (Volver a hablar de un tema después): 
- Retomar un tema de conversación más tarde. 
Ej: I don't have the answer right now, but I'll CIRCLE BACK to you next week. 

7. Low-hanging fruit (La oportunidad más fácil o rápida): 
- Las tareas o ventas más fáciles de conseguir con el menor esfuerzo. 
Ej: Instead of chasing massive clients, let's target the LOW-HANGING FRUIT first.
parts.audio: Number 4: Get the ball rolling. To start a process or project. For example: Let's GET THE BALL ROLLING on the new software update. Number 5: Kick the can down the road. To delay making a difficult decision, hoping it goes away or dealing with it later. For example: The politicians didn't solve the debt crisis; they just KICKED THE CAN DOWN THE ROAD. Number 6: Circle back. To return to a topic or person later. For example: I don't have the answer right now, but I'll CIRCLE BACK to you next week. Number 7: Low-hanging fruit. The easiest tasks to complete or sales to make with minimal effort. For example: Instead of chasing massive clients, let's target the LOW-HANGING FRUIT first.

questions.question: Changing the font on our website is fine, but it really isn't going to move the ____ in terms of overall sales. (Mover la aguja / Hacer la diferencia).
questions.explanation: Move the needle = lograr un cambio o impacto notable.

questions.question: Let's start by addressing the local problems first; we don't need to ____ the ocean on day one. (Abarcar demasiado / Intentar lo imposible).
questions.explanation: Boil the ocean = intentar algo ridículamente grande o imposible.

questions.question: Apple became a massive success because Steve Jobs always wanted to ____ the envelope with design. (Ir más allá de los límites).
questions.explanation: Push the envelope = innovar, ir al límite.

questions.question: Instead of delaying the budget cuts again, we need to act now. We can't just keep kicking the ____ down the road. (Posponer el problema).
questions.explanation: Kick the can down the road = posponer un problema para el futuro.

questions.question: I don't have the final numbers right now, but let's ____ back to this topic after lunch. (Retomar el tema).
questions.explanation: Circle back = retomar una conversación más tarde.

questions.question: To get some quick wins this quarter, our sales team should focus entirely on the ____-hanging fruit. (Lo más fácil de conseguir).
questions.explanation: Low-hanging fruit = la oportunidad que requiere el menor esfuerzo.

questions.question: We need someone to take charge and get the ____ rolling on the marketing campaign. (Empezar/Poner en marcha).
questions.explanation: Get the ball rolling = iniciar un proceso.

questions.question: When everyone is on the same ____, the team works much more efficiently. (Estar de acuerdo / En sintonía).
questions.explanation: On the same page = estar de acuerdo o tener la misma información básica.

questions.question: The CEO told us to think outside the ____ to find a creative solution. (Pensar de forma original).
questions.explanation: Think outside the box = pensar de forma creativa.

questions.question: We don't need a detailed explanation right now, just give me the ____-picture overview. (Visión general).
questions.explanation: Big picture = la visión general o el contexto más amplio.

questions.question: I'll let you handle the negotiations; it's entirely in your ____. (En tu terreno / Tu responsabilidad).
questions.explanation: In someone's wheelhouse = el área de especialidad o control de alguien.

questions.question: The manager asked me to bring him up to ____ on the current status of the merger. (Actualizar/Poner al día).
questions.explanation: Bring someone up to speed = actualizar a alguien con la última información.

questions.question: We need to make sure this new app is entirely up to ____ before we release it. (Al nivel esperado / Estándar).
questions.explanation: Up to par = alcanzar el nivel, estándar o calidad mínima requerida.

questions.question: Let's touch ____ next Monday to see how the project is progressing. (Hablar brevemente / Contactar).
questions.explanation: Touch base = hacer contacto breve para actualizarse.

questions.question: The deal is completely up in the ____ right now; we don't know if they will sign or not. (En el aire / Incierto).
questions.explanation: Up in the air = incierto, aún no decidido.

questions.question: We are losing money every day. It's time to pull the ____ on this project. (Cancelar / Poner fin).
questions.explanation: Pull the plug = detener, cancelar o quitar el financiamiento a un proyecto.

questions.question: The competitor caught us off ____ with their sudden price drop. (Desprevenidos).
questions.explanation: Catch someone off guard = sorprender a alguien desprevenido.

questions.question: He has a lot on his ____ right now, so don't give him any more tasks. (Estar muy ocupado / Tener muchas responsabilidades).
questions.explanation: Have a lot on one's plate = tener muchas responsabilidades o problemas a la vez.

questions.question: At the ____ of the day, profitability is all that matters to the shareholders. (Al fin y al cabo / En conclusión).
questions.explanation: At the end of the day = al final, lo más importante es...

questions.question: We are trying to find a ____-win situation for both the union and the management. (Donde ambos ganan).
questions.explanation: Win-win situation = situación beneficiosa para ambas partes.

questions.explanation: page.

questions.explanation: plug.

questions.explanation: base.
